call.text: The routing module decides chunk boundaries by measuring cosine similarity between adjacent encoder outputs and converting this similarity into a boundary probability p_t that is high when similarity is low [HNET:2.2.1:c023]. Specifically, it computes q_t = W_q ĥx_t and k_t = W_k ĥx_t, then sets p_t = ½ (1 − (q_tᵀ k_{t‑1}) / ‖q_t‖ ‖k_{t‑1}‖) which lies in [0, 1] [HNET:2.2.1:c023]. A hard boundary indicator b_t is obtained by thresholding p_t at 0.5, i.e., b_t = 1 if p_t ≥ 0.5 else 0, with p_1 defined as 1.0 to start the sequence with a boundary [HNET:2.2.1:c023]. This mechanism implements the intuition that meaningful boundaries emerge where contextual or semantic shift causes lower similarity between consecutive vectors [HNET:1:c007].
